setup: Sit on the edge of a stable bench
Hands beside your hips, fingers forward
Slide your hips just off the front edge
Knees bent, feet flat on the floor
execution: Bend your elbows and lower straight down
Keep your back close to the bench
Stop at about a right angle at the elbow
Press through your palms to straighten
faults: Don't sink until your shoulders roll forward
Don't let your elbows flare wide
Don't drift away from the bench

notes: Use a bench or box that can't slide or tip. A gym bench against a wall or rack is safest.
Depth is the main lever. Going deeper than a comfortable elbow bend puts the front of the shoulder in a stretched, loaded position; stop short of that.
Bent knees make it easier; straight legs or feet raised make it harder. Change the leg position before adding load.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain at the front of the shoulder
Pain that changes how you move
Numbness or tingling in the hands

regressions.name: Bench dip with feet close
regressions.reason: Knees bent and feet near the bench take more of your weight through the legs.

regressions.name: Assisted dip
regressions.reason: Upright dip with the machine taking some of your weight; easy to load in small steps.

progressions.name: Bench dip with straight legs
progressions.reason: Heels further away puts more of your weight on the arms.

progressions.name: Bench dip with feet raised
progressions.reason: Feet on a second bench makes the arms carry most of your weight.

progressions.name: Dip
progressions.reason: The arms carry all your bodyweight on parallel bars.

substitutions.name: Triceps pushdown
substitutions.reason: Triceps work on a cable stack with no shoulder stretch at the bottom.

substitutions.name: Diamond push-up
substitutions.reason: Triceps-focused bodyweight press with no bench needed.

substitutions.name: Close-grip bench press
substitutions.reason: Heavier, loadable triceps press; needs a rack and bench.

substitutions.name: Assisted dip
substitutions.reason: Dip pattern on a machine; load is assistance, so a larger number is easier.

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view at bench height, figure facing right with the bench behind. Shows the elbow bend, the hips travelling straight down close to the bench edge, and the shoulder position at the bottom.

keyPositions.label: Top
keyPositions.describe: Arms straight, hands on the bench edge beside the hips, fingers forward. Hips just in front of the bench. Knees bent to about 90°, feet flat. Chest up, shoulders down away from the ears.

keyPositions.label: Bottom
keyPositions.describe: Elbows bent to about 90°, pointing straight back. Hips have dropped straight down, back close to the bench. Chest still up; shoulders not rolled forward.

ikHints: Hands fixed on the bench edge in every frame
emphasise: Hips travel straight down, close to the bench
Bottom stops at about a right angle at the elbow
doNotShow: Very deep dip with shoulders rolled forward
Hips drifting far from the bench
